description: Gating backfill program (81-band). A quality pass over the gates the backfill generates: audit them for fabricated or trivial questions and tighten the grader so backfilled gates hold the SAME bar as hand-built ones, keeping the reference-`solution`-run-against-its-own-`test` subprocess verification the load-bearing check before a gate may be written. This is the gating-side analogue of construct.py's construction_failures discipline: tighten THIS grader when a new fabrication is found, keep its sentences specific (they are the repair prompt and the UI's error text). The risk backfill-at-scale introduces is a gate that technically validates but asks nothing real — a choice question whose answer is given away, a short question the rubric already answers, a code check whose test asserts nothing meaningful — and this band is the guard against it. REVISED 2026-08-11 by decision D10 (../ADOPT-DECIDE-REGISTER.md): the artifact being audited is now 84's adopted nbgrader schema, and `nbgrader validate` is the AUTHORITATIVE gate — so this band's job is precisely the residue validate does NOT cover. That distinction is the whole point: nbgrader proves a graded cell is wellformed and that its hidden tests execute against its solution; it CANNOT tell you the question is trivial, that the answer is given away in the prompt, or that the test asserts nothing meaningful. Praxis's grader owns exactly that gap and must not re-litigate what validate already decides. Depends on 84 (the schema and the validate gate) and on the batched-gating story (79), whose output it audits. Anti-fabrication IS the deliverable: a fabricated or trivial gate is rejected and never written, and a test proves a deliberately trivial/fabricated one is caught while a genuine one passes.
warmup: echo '--- the grader to tighten, and its load-bearing verify_code half ---'; sed -n '362,420p' praxis/checks.py
echo '--- the sibling discipline on the construction side ---'; grep -n 'def construction_failures\|def gate_failures\|fabricat' praxis/rubric.py | head
echo '--- the rule that carries the weight: solution run against its own test ---'; grep -n 'verify_code\|subprocess\|solution\|def _run' praxis/checks.py | head

userStories.title: Audit backfilled checksets for fabricated or trivial questions
acceptanceCriteria: An audit pass scans the checksets produced by the 79 backfill for the failure modes scale introduces — an answer given away in the prompt, a short-answer the notebook body already answers verbatim, a code check whose test asserts nothing, a duplicated/near-identical question across sections — and reports each with a specific reason.

The audit reuses the shipped signals (the write-path grader's shape, the GATED_SECTIONS coverage, the solution-against-its-own-test subprocess result) rather than a parallel grader, so it measures the same thing the write path enforces — and it audits ONLY the residue `nbgrader validate` does not cover (triviality, an answer given away, a test that asserts nothing), never re-implementing validate's wellformedness or execution checks.
Gate green: python3 -m pytest -q tests/ passes, including a test that the audit flags a deliberately trivial/fabricated fixture checkset and passes a genuine one.

userStories.title: Tighten checkset_failures so a trivial set can never be written
acceptanceCriteria: The write-path grader is tightened so the fabrication/triviality modes the audit found are caught at write time — a gate exhibiting one is rejected and never written (same rule as the constructor), with the solution-against-its-own-test subprocess run kept as the load-bearing check, and `nbgrader validate` still the authoritative gate it runs ALONGSIDE rather than replaces.

The new failure sentences are specific enough to act on (they feed the repair prompt and surface as the UI's error text), and the cheap load path stays cheap — the tightening lands only on the write/verify path.

Gate green: python3 -m pytest -q tests/ covers the tightened rules — asserting a fabricated/trivial gate is rejected with an actionable message and that the existing hand-built seed gates still pass (no regression to the 24 already gated).

userStories.title: Re-audit checksets written before the tightened bar, and regenerate only by policy
acceptanceCriteria: A re-audit pass runs the tightened grader over every gate already on disk that was written BEFORE the tightening landed (79 batches may run before this band merges), reporting each one that no longer meets the bar with the grader's specific sentence — measuring with the same tightened write-path grader, never a parallel one.

The gate rules are respected: an already-gated notebook is skipped, not rewritten — a pre-tightening gate that now fails is FLAGGED for regeneration, and regeneration is an explicit per-notebook pass through the shipped checks.py write path (grade-then-write, plus `nbgrader validate`), so a regenerated gate that fails the tightened bar is never written and the existing one stays in place rather than leaving the notebook ungated.

Gate green: python3 -m pytest -q tests/ passes, including a test that the re-audit flags a fixture gate failing only the NEW rules while leaving it on disk untouched, and that an explicit regeneration replaces it only with one passing the tightened bar.
